title: His first frisbee
text: Scout discovered his love for playing fetch pretty early on, thanks to a spur-of-the-moment decision to buy him an ultimate frisbee. We were visiting relatives at my family's farm in Spring Hill, Kansas, and I started throwing it out into the field behind the house. He took to it almost immediately. Before long, the word frisbee had become permanently etched into his vocabulary, and it quickly became his favorite thing in the world.

title: Playing fetch until he dropped
text:
Whenever you would say the word frisbee, his face would immediately light up with intense interest.  It didn't matter if he was sleeping, eating food, entirely engrossed in some other thing, he'd immediately look up at you like he was saying "I'm ready, let's go".

I still remember, even being at my parents house, where he did the majority of his frisbee fetching, from the moment he walked in he was ready to get the frisbee and go right back outside.  In fact he really wouldn't leave you alone until he got a few throws in.

He'd spend hours over the years running back and forth across their property, from the sloped, hilly backyard all the way to the cul-de-sac out front, chasing frisbees until he was completely worn out.  There were many times that I had to make him stop, because I was afraid he would push himself to hard and get hurt or worse.

title: The bucket
text: When he'd get worn out and thirsty, he'd head over to a bucket my parents kept underneath the hose faucet in the front yard. He'd stick his frisbee in the bucket and start gulping down water. Once he'd had enough and was ready to go back to playing, he'd start putting his paw in the bucket, twirling the frisbee around and sloshing all the water out. I still don't understand what exactly compelled him to do that, but we spent many hot summer afternoons enjoying this silly little routine.

title: The Chattahoochee
text: Swimming was another one of his favorite pastimes. We made countless trips to various parks along the Chattahoochee River, bringing along a water frisbee or, if we didn't have one, a good old stick we'd find somewhere along the trail. He'd happily run in and out of the water, chasing whatever I threw for him, seemingly never getting tired of it. Those simple afternoons became some of my favorite memories with him.

title: Running buddies
text: Scout would also frequently accompany me on runs along the Chattahoochee, provided there were enough spots along the way where he could get into the water and cool off if it was too hot outside. He absolutely loved coming with me, and he loved our stops by the river even more, since that meant he got to play fetch for a few throws before we continued on our way. It was a nice way for us to spend time together, and I always enjoyed having him along for the ride.

title: The rock collector
text: Another interesting activity he developed a liking for was dunking his entire head underwater to retrieve whatever he could find on the bottom. Usually, it was a rock, but really, anything submerged was fair game. The bigger the object, the better. He'd plunge his head underwater, come back up with whatever he found, carry it to shore, drop it on the ground, and go right back for another one. He'd repeat the process over and over until he'd accumulated a little collection of rocks and other miscellaneous items along the water's edge, typically in one big pile. I always found it funny how determined he was to collect these things, as if he had some sort of important job to do.

title: Chasing his tail
text: I also remember how much he loved chasing his tail when he was younger. I didn't really have a problem with it, other than worrying he might hurt himself or knock something over, so I eventually taught him that chasing his tail was something he shouldn't do. Of course, that didn't actually stop him. I remember he'd start sneaking into other rooms just so he could chase his tail without being seen. I even caught him doing it once on the cameras at his puppy playgroup, where I'd drop him off every once in a while while I was at work. There he was, in the middle of a big room full of other dogs playing with each other, and he'd apparently decided it was the perfect opportunity to chase his tail!

title: Room for one more
text:
Scout also absolutely loved sitting on any seat that could fit more than just him. Whether it was a couch, a big bench, or even a chair he could somehow squeeze himself onto beside you, he wanted to be right there with everyone else. My parents have a swing on their back porch, and as soon as someone would sit down on it, if Scout knew about it, he'd be right up there with them, swinging back and forth and just enjoying his time.

I know a lot of people don't let their dogs get up on the furniture, but for some reason, I never really felt compelled to teach Scout that it wasn't okay. I just wanted him to feel like he belonged. And while it may have cost me a couch or two over the years, I feel like it was worth it to have a companion who really felt like part of the pack. He may have been a dog, but in his head, he was one of us. He was a person, and I always tried to treat him with the utmost respect.
